Subject: Performance SLO & Private VPC qualification — next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Recap + concrete next steps below so we can line up network/SE time and a short PoC window.

Key requirements you confirmed on the call:
- Latency: p95 inference response target <= 150ms for typical requests (~1k token workloads).
- Streaming: server-side streaming required for chat (expect partial token flushes to client).
- Concurrency/Throughput: expect sustained 300-500 concurrent open sessions with peak bursts up to ~1,200 RPS for short windows; average throughput ~1k requests/minute.
- Networking: private VPC/on-prem connectivity (VPN or dedicated peering), strict egress IP allowlist, and internal latency budget between frontend app and inference endpoint ideally < 20ms.

What we (Redwood) will provide for qualification:
1) VPC qualification checklist (attached: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf) — includes ports, TLS, and keepalive settings.
2) Test endpoints + predictable egress IPs for firewall allowlisting.
3) Suggestions for streaming flush/buffer settings (SE notes below).
4) A suggested 1-week PoC: canary traffic to a Private deployment or dedicated pool; we’ll instrument token-level latency and bandwidth.

Requests from ACME for next steps:
- Please send your network diagram and firewall policy (NAT, proxy, VPN terminator) and the list of egress IPs that can be whitelisted.
- Can your networking team share the expected internal latency budget (app -> inference endpoint) and whether you have existing private peering (Partner colo / AWS Direct Connect / GCP Interconnect) or plan to use IPsec VPN with NAT?
- If possible, share a short pcap/traceroute from one app host to the intended endpoint. We can use that to check MTU, TCP MSS and any middlebox issues.

Tentative next actions I propose:
- ACME networking provides diagram + egress IPs (by EOD Tue).
- Redwood SE (Marissa) to run a quick latency test once IPs/hostnames are provided, and propose any TCP/TLS tuning.
- Schedule a 60-min network workshop with ACME Net team (please propose 2 slots).
- Set up a 1-week canary PoC after configs are validated.

I’m copying Marissa/Aditya from SE/AM so they can pick this up. If you can drop the network diagram and firewall policy now, we’ll start triage immediately.

Thanks — Jordan

Thanks Sam — quick technical notes from SE perspective: 
- Streaming: Redwood supports HTTP/2 streaming and HTTP/1.1 chunked responses; for client-side behavior we recommend HTTP/2 where possible due to lower head-of-line blocking. For chat-style UX we flush partial tokens to the client roughly every 100-250ms depending on batch size and tokenization.
- Latency p95: the target Jordan noted is for full-response latency for ~1k token responses. If you have many shorter responses we’ll expect substantially lower p95s.
- Peering: for initial qualification static routes + IPsec VPN is fine. For production at scale we typically recommend dedicated peering (BGP) to reduce NAT/session churn, but we can validate via VPN for the PoC.
- TCP/TLS tuning: enable keepalives, configure idle timeouts > 120s, ensure MTU >= 1500 across path, and avoid inline proxies that buffer streaming responses.

If you can share a traceroute and a small pcap (10-20s) from an app host to the target endpoint we’ll run a quick MTU/TCP MSS analysis and report back. We can also provide a test hostname and fixed egress IPs to include in your firewall.

I can take the network workshop once we have the diagram — propose Tue 2028-05-21 09:00 or 14:00 PT. Which works for Net team?

Thanks — Marissa
